    Bullish Quasimodo (QM)

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of a downtrend and resembles an inverse head and shoulders. After making a new low, price breaks structure with a close above the previous high, then comes back to the level of the left shoulder's low. That level is called the QM level; price leaving a higher low there can signal that the downtrend has ended.

    How it forms

    1. Prior downtrend. The pattern is a reversal signal. It needs a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows before it.
    2. Left shoulder (L). Price makes a low and rises to a high (H). The left shoulder's low will later be the QM level.
    3. Head (LL). Price moves below the left shoulder to a lower low. This low is often a reach that collects the stops and resting orders below the left shoulder.
    4. Break of structure (HH). Price rises sharply from the head and closes above the H high. The downtrend's protected high has broken (MSB / CHoCH); this becomes the new, higher high (HH).
    5. Right shoulder. Price falls again and approaches the QM level, the left shoulder's low. There it leaves a higher low that stays above the head.
    6. Completion. Price turns from the right shoulder and the rise continues. Until the right shoulder forms, the pattern is only forming.

    What it suggests

    The head is the downtrend's last new low. The break of structure with a close that follows shows that the high sellers were defending has been lost. When price returns to the QM level at the right shoulder, the level where buyers acted at the left shoulder is tested again; price staying above the head there can signal that the new direction is up.

    The difference from an inverse head and shoulders is the order: in an inverse head and shoulders the right shoulder forms first and the neckline breaks after. In a QM structure breaks first, and the right shoulder is the return that comes after the break.

    When it strengthens, when it weakens

    Strengthens

    • The head forming at a support zone or with a clear sweep
    • The break of structure (HH) coming with strong, large-bodied candles
    • The QM level lining up with a demand zone or an order block
    • The right shoulder being the first return to the QM level
    • The downtrend also losing strength on a larger timeframe

    Weakens

    • No close above the H high; only a wick through it
    • The right shoulder clearly moving past the QM level towards the head
    • No clear downtrend before it
    • A strong downtrend continuing on a larger timeframe

    The MarketLevelMap view

    How it relates to zones

    A QM has two critical places, and both mean more when read together with zones:

    • If the QM level (the left shoulder's low) lines up with a support or demand zone, the turn at the right shoulder means more.
    • If the head forms with a wick just below a support zone and turns back, the move can be read as a sweep.

    In MarketLevelMap's Price Action view, breaks of structure are shown with CHoCH and BOS labels, and range edges that were passed with a wick and returned to are shown with a Sweep label. The head and the break of structure steps of a QM can be followed with these labels.

    When it completes

    After the break of structure, a higher low (the right shoulder) at the QM level, then a rise.

    When it is invalidated

    Before completion: If, after the break of structure, price does not stop at the QM level, keeps falling and closes below the head, the pattern is considered not to have formed.

    After completion: Even if the rise from the right shoulder has started, a drop back with a close below the head invalidates the bullish scenario.

    Often confused with

    • Bearish Quasimodo (QM)The mirrored version: a new high at the end of an uptrend, a downward break of structure and a return to the QM level.
    • Inverse Head and ShouldersIn an inverse head and shoulders the right shoulder forms first and the neckline breaks after; in a QM structure breaks first and the right shoulder comes after.
    • CHoCH: change of characterThe break of structure in a QM is a CHoCH; a QM also covers price returning to the left shoulder's level after that break.
